I see the source of confusion.

The "free fall" of the WTC 7 building described by Stage 2 is the North Face only. Yes, this section of the building's columns were falling during that time frame as a sufficient number of columns had buckled along the North Face's column line due to the fire (all objects fall at gravitational acceleration regardless of any other condition). This does not mean that the entire building was in a state of free fall, only the specific columns and attached beams along that column line.

For the entire building to be in a state of free fall, all the supporting columns must be severed at the same time (hence the floor by floor detonation of demolition charges which are seen in controlled demolitions). This is generally what people are referring to when they claim that the WTC buildings were in free fall, and where they are absolutely wrong about it. In WTC 7's case, the column line along the North Face collapsed after the penthouses did (as illustrated in Figure 3-10 to 13). As the structure collapsed, load is shifted through the structure to the surviving beams and columns (who are also damaged due to the fire), subsequently overloading them. This is of course very simplified explanation-wise, as there are all kinds of things going on with impact damage and dynamic load changes. This is what is referred to by the term progressive collapse, one element failure results in adjacent element failures.

As pointed out on page 45, if the entire building had been in a state of free fall, the upper 18 stores would have collapsed in 3.9 seconds. It was not, as the video showed, collapsing instead in 5.4 seconds. So yes, elements of the building were in a state of free fall at certain given instances in time, however none of the buildings, in their entirety, were in a state of free fall at any given point, as would be the case in a controlled demolition.

The problem comes in the failure of laymen understanding this. It is a very important distinction to make.

From a dilution standpoint this is very good, because it means that all the heavy metals stay at fairly low concentrations.
